items.title: 52060_Eddie Barefield oral history interview
items.q: I went in there with the trio, with Norman Simmons and -- well, it's a quartet -- Norman Simmons and Eddie Locke and [Vic] Sproles Vic Sproles, a bass player.

ctx.x: That's right. But today it's all Holiday Inn or some facsimile. And then the -- after I come back from Europe with Red, I took a trip out to see my sister in Des Moines. And then in 1970 Ty Ree Glenn Tyree Glenn was working at the Roundtable, and he took a vacation, so I went in there with the trio, with Norman Simmons and -- well, it's a quartet -- Norman Simmons and Eddie Locke and [Vic] Sproles Vic Sproles, a bass player. That was a

nice couple of weeks.
And then I went to Cleveland that same year with Red -- Richard at the Theatrical Grill. We went to -- also went to Pittsburgh. There was a place in Pittsburgh -- we played in a hotel called Basin Street. And then I went out that same year with Georgie Jessel and his show. And we played -- then I played -- we had some schools, and we were playing jazz out to a lot of the schools in Long Island, which we do some now, still do.
